messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for service=inference-runtime-prod severity=critical — high 5xx rate on /v1/generate across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Incident auto-grouped alerts into a single incident.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC12345 created, triggered by alert 'runtime_high_error_rate'. Assigned to: maria. Escalation policy: oncall-sre -> eng-lead after 10m.

maria: ACK. I'm jumping in, looking at logs now. Can someone drop SLO dashboards? :eyes: 

akshay: pulling metrics — 5xx spikes started ~2026-11-03T02:10:00Z, error rate ~12% for 30m, p50 latency ↑ 40ms. Seems correlated with a config push to batching in the runtime at 02:08.

lia: we rolled a batching change (reduce max_batch_wait to 8ms) at 02:05, rollback flagged as candidate.

maria: good catch. Trying quick rollback to previous batching profile now. Will post command and logs.

maria: 
```
# rollback to previous batching profile
redwoodctl runtime update --deployment inference-prod --batch-config previous_profile
```

maria: rollback initiated, will take ~45s per node. Noticing immediate drop in queue latency.

derek: FYI I'm getting paged repeatedly — looks like alert duplicates flooding oncall. PD is sending multiple alerts for same symptom across clusters. Paging storm is noisy.

incident-bot: Alert dedupe attempted: grouping key=alertname:runtime_high_error_rate, labels={region,instance}. Current grouping grouped 14 alerts into INC12345 but multiple distinct alert fingerprints still causing repeated pages.

akshay: we should silence the noisy alerts while we mitigate. Adding a 30m silence scoped to the alertname + incident tag.

lia: how are you adding silence? We should use alertmanager so PD doesn't re-fire.

amended commands for context: 
```
amtool silence add --match 'alertname="runtime_high_error_rate"' --starts 'now' --ends 'now+30m' --comment 'silence during rollback and mitigation' --created-by maria
```

maria: silence added via amtool, verifying PD stops sending duplicates.

pagerduty-bot: Silence acknowledged. Suppression applied to alerts matching alertname=runtime_high_error_rate for 30m.

derek: duplicates reduced, thanks. Still seeing one alert per region which is fine.

akshay: rollback finished on 12/12 nodes, traffic shifted back to stable batching. Error rate trending down to 1.8% in us-east-1. Continuing monitor.

maria: quick customer impact note for handoff: ~10% of requests between 02:10-02:35 saw 5xx, ~0.6% of total platform traffic affected, customers might've seen timeouts/retries. No major data loss. Temporary mitigation: pinned routing to older model variant and rolled back batching.

lia: adding a Jira: RED-7892 with reproducible steps + links to dashboards and rollback diff.

maria: handing off to akshay for the next 30m watch. I'm out for a short break, leave a note in the incident timeline. @akshay please take over — summary pinned.

akshay: ACK takeover. I'll keep guard for 30m, will reopen if error rate rises >3% over 5m. Will also follow up after incident for dedupe tuning.

incident-bot: Incident INC12345 updated: status=mitigated, assignee=akshay, note='Rollback applied; silence added; monitoring.'

akshay: quick follow-up action items for postmortem: 1) tighten alert grouping key to drop instance-level noise; 2) increase dedupe window from 5m to 10m for runtime_high_error_rate; 3) add preflight check for batching config that simulates tail latency.

maria: +1 on all. Also suggest run a short chaos test for batching changes in staging.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation timer stopped; no further escalations.

akshay: monitoring looks stable for 22m, reducing paging policy heat. Will close incident once stable for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident INC12345 resolved by akshay. Root cause suspected: aggressive batching config change reduced processing headroom causing increased queue time and 5xx under peak bursts. Follow-up: RED-7892 assigned, owner=lia.

maria: thanks team — solid coordination. Leaving a short handoff note in #incidents and updating runbook with a new checklist for batching rollouts. :white_check_mark:

derek: nice work.

akshay: closing thread, will post postmortem draft in ~24h.
